geography.notes: Nebraska statewide tax incentive; Tier 5 renewable electricity project applications closed to new applicants after December 31, 2020.

hardRequirements: Project must qualify as renewable electricity production for sale under the Nebraska Advantage Act Tier 5 rules.
Tier 5 projects required at least $20 million investment in qualified property.
Only existing approved agreements remain relevant because new Tier 5 applications closed after December 31, 2020.
blockers: No new applications are accepted for this incentive tier.
Ground-source geothermal heat pumps are not supported by the statute; geothermal is listed as an electricity-production source, not building HVAC.
Residential or ordinary building retrofits do not qualify unless part of a qualified business renewable electricity project.
repairs.evidenceText: Nebraska]( law treated Tier 5 renewable projects as qualified businesses only for electricity production for sale from sources including wind, solar, geothermal, hydroelectric, and biomass; no new Tier 5 applications could be filed after December 31, 2020.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Keep only renewable electric-generation categories. Block the matched geothermal heat pump category because the statute does not support building HVAC retrofits.

geography.notes: Connecticut statewide sales-and-use-tax exemption.

hardRequirements: Purchaser must complete Connecticut CERT-140 for qualifying purchases.
System must be a solar electricity generating system, passive or active solar water or space heating system, or geothermal resource system.
Exemption can cover qualifying equipment and installation services when statutory conditions are met.
blockers: Do not match non-geothermal HVAC, ordinary water heaters, or building weatherization.
Ice storage and other demand-management equipment are separate topics unless specifically listed as part of the qualified exemption.
Solar or geothermal equipment must fall within the Connecticut exemption; unrelated renewable equipment is not supported here.
repairs.evidenceText: Connecticut]( DRS lists solar electricity, passive or active solar water or space heating, and geothermal resource systems as sales-and-use-tax exempt when the purchaser completes CERT-140.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The supplied geothermal and solar-water-heating matches are source-backed. Added rooftop PV and solar space heating because the official exemption expressly supports them.

geography.notes: Connecticut statewide industry-focused sales-and-use-tax exemption.

hardRequirements: Purchaser must be engaged in renewable or clean energy technology industries.
Items must be used directly in eligible renewable or clean-energy technology activities.
Purchaser must use the applicable Connecticut exemption certificate for the industry exemption.
blockers: This is not an end-user building retrofit incentive for installing geothermal heat pumps or solar water heaters.
Real property, fixtures, services, repair and replacement parts, administration, and general management uses are excluded.
Do not match building-level solar thermal or geothermal retrofits from this industry support exemption.
repairs.evidenceText: The]( special notice covers machinery, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, and fuel used directly by renewable or clean-energy technology companies; it excludes real property, fixtures, services, and nonproduction uses.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Clear retrofit categories because the current official source supports industry inputs, not installation of geothermal or solar-thermal systems in buildings.

geography.notes: Illinois statewide program for certified High Impact Businesses and designated large energy facilities.

hardRequirements: Business must qualify and be certified under the Illinois High Impact Business Program.
Standard High Impact Business qualifications require major investment and job creation or retention thresholds.
Energy facility eligibility is limited to designated wind, new utility-scale solar, and new battery energy storage solution facilities.
blockers: Not a customer-sited rooftop solar or home battery rebate.
Solar-plus-storage should not be matched unless the project is a qualifying utility-scale solar or battery energy storage facility.
Certification must occur before project commencement and before qualifying purchases.
repairs.administrator: Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity
repairs.evidenceText: DCEO]( describes High Impact Business as a large-scale business incentive expanded to wind, utility-scale solar, and new battery energy storage solution facilities.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Narrow battery and solar matches to utility-scale facility categories. Block residential, small commercial, and generic solar-plus-storage interpretations.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying SMPA members in the cooperative service territory.

hardRequirements: Installation must be in SMPA territory and connected to the grid.
Renewable system must be owned by the SMPA member to qualify.
Solar PV must use listed or approved grid-tied inverters.
Small wind systems must be grid-tied, listed or approved, and SWCC-certified where required.
Contractor application and program deadlines apply.
blockers: Off-grid systems are not supported by the rebate requirements.
Third-party lease arrangements without member ownership interest do not qualify.
Do not broaden to unrelated renewable measures beyond listed solar PV, small wind, and any separately listed hydro measures.
repairs.evidenceText: SMPA]( lists residential and commercial PV rebates and residential small-wind rebates, with grid-tied equipment and member-ownership requirements.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The matched rooftop solar PV and small wind categories are source-backed. Territory, ownership, grid-tie, and equipment requirements are critical matching constraints.

geography.notes: Available to approved Santee Cooper customers; loan checks are issued directly to the approved trade ally or installer.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be an approved Santee Cooper customer and qualify for financing.
Renewable Energy Resource Loan can support qualifying solar PV, wind, micro-hydro, or biomass generation.
Work must be completed through program processes, including approved trade ally or installer payment requirements.
Solar projects must satisfy applicable interconnection and program requirements.
blockers: This is financing, not a rebate or grant.
Biomass eligibility is for renewable generation, not broad biomass heating or building-fuel conversion.
Commercial projects are not supported by the residential EmpowerHome loan page unless covered by a separate business program.
repairs.evidenceText: Santee]( Cooper describes low-interest loans for residential energy upgrades and renewable generation, including solar panels and Renewable Energy Resource Loans for solar PV, wind, micro-hydro, and biomass generation.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Keep rooftop solar PV and biomass only as financed renewable generation. Do not treat the loan as a rebate-style retrofit incentive.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying Satilla REMC residential members and homeowners.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be a Satilla REMC member or otherwise meet program homeowner qualifications.
Project must pass Satilla REMC prescreening where required.
Financing must be approved through Go Energy Financial Credit Union or the current program lender.
Work must use eligible improvements and program processes.
blockers: This is a loan program, not a rebate or grant.
Commercial and industrial applicants are not supported by the HomePlus residential loan page.
Generators, roofs, windows, and HVAC are separate financed item types and should not broaden weatherization matching.
repairs.evidenceText: Satilla]( REMC says HomePlus loans finance energy-efficient home improvements, including insulation and weatherization, subject to EMC prescreening and loan approval.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The matched insulation and weatherization categories are supported, but should be treated as financed residential measures only.

geography.notes: Available within Seattle city limits and, for some electrically heated income-qualified homes, to Seattle City Light customers outside city limits.

hardRequirements: Household must meet income eligibility requirements.
Home must be within Seattle limits or meet Seattle City Light electric-heat eligibility outside the city.
Weatherization measures depend on audit or inspection findings.
Rental and multifamily participation may require property owner cooperation and tenant income qualification.
blockers: Not available statewide in Washington.
Commercial buildings are not supported by the HomeWise residential weatherization page.
Some non-envelope measures, such as heat pumps or water heaters, are inspection- or equipment-condition-dependent and should not be generalized from the envelope match.
repairs.evidenceText: Seattle]( HomeWise provides free energy-efficiency improvements to income-qualified homes, including insulation and duct or air sealing, with eligibility limited by location, income, and program inspection.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The air sealing and insulation matches are source-backed. Geography and income limits are essential blockers for deterministic matching.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying SHELD electric customers.

hardRequirements: Customer must enroll in the SHELD NextZero Scheduled Charging Program for the required term.
Eligible charger must be an approved networked charger, such as listed Emporia or ChargePoint models.
Charger must be installed by a licensed contractor or electrician where required.
Permit, wiring inspection, application, and participation agreement requirements may apply.
blockers: Do not match as a generic EV charger rebate without the Level 2 and scheduled-charging requirements.
Not an EV purchase rebate.
Unsupported charger brands and nonparticipating customers do not qualify.
Commercial charger incentives are not supported by this residential SHELD page.
repairs.evidenceText: SHELD]( offers a residential EV charger rebate after successful participation in its NextZero Scheduled Charging Program and requires approved chargers and proper installation.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Narrow the match to Level 2 EV charger installation with scheduled-charging participation. Generic EVSE matching is too broad without those requirements.

geography.notes: Hawaii statewide income tax credit for qualifying corporate taxpayers; future-year rules may change under Act 24 of 2026.

hardRequirements: Claimant must be a qualifying Hawaii corporate taxpayer.
System must be a qualifying renewable energy technology system installed and placed in service in Hawaii.
Taxpayer must claim the credit through the required Hawaii tax forms and comply with cost caps, output capacity rules, and allocation requirements.
blockers: This is a tax credit, not a rebate.
Standalone battery storage is not supported by the corporate solar and wind credit match.
Wind is separately eligible but should not be conflated with solar PV or solar water heating categories.
Eligibility and credit amount may change for taxable years affected by Act 24 of 2026.
repairs.evidenceText: Hawaii]( tax guidance describes the Renewable Energy Technologies Income Tax Credit for qualifying solar PV, solar space heating, and solar thermal water-heating systems, subject to statutory caps and rules.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The matched rooftop solar PV and solar water heating categories are supported. Added solar space heating because Hawaii guidance groups it with qualifying solar technologies.

geography.notes: Hawaii statewide income tax credit for qualifying individual taxpayers; future-year rules may change under Act 24 of 2026.

hardRequirements: Claimant must be a qualifying Hawaii individual taxpayer.
System must be a qualifying renewable energy technology system installed and placed in service in Hawaii.
Taxpayer must claim the credit through the required Hawaii tax forms and comply with cost caps, output capacity rules, and allocation requirements.
blockers: This is a tax credit, not an upfront rebate.
Standalone battery storage is not supported by the personal solar and wind credit match.
Wind is separately eligible but should not be conflated with solar PV or solar water heating categories.
Eligibility and credit amount may change for taxable years affected by Act 24 of 2026.
repairs.evidenceText: Hawaii]( tax guidance describes the Renewable Energy Technologies Income Tax Credit for qualifying solar PV, solar space heating, and solar thermal water-heating systems, subject to statutory caps and rules.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The matched rooftop solar PV and solar water heating categories are supported for individual taxpayers. Added solar space heating because it is explicitly within the qualifying solar technologies.

geography.notes: Arizona statewide transaction privilege tax deduction for qualifying solar energy devices sold by registered retailers or lessors.

hardRequirements: Retailer or lessor must register with the Arizona Department of Revenue as a solar energy retailer or lessor.
Sale or lease must be of a qualifying solar energy device under Arizona law.
Retailer must maintain records supporting the deduction from the tax base.
blockers: Submetering or energy monitoring is not a supported retrofit category unless it is integral to a qualifying solar energy device.
Standalone metering, monitoring, storage, and non-solar controls do not qualify under this program match.
Current official solar-device sources do not support a standalone wind-equipment match for this Arizona sales-tax deduction.
repairs.evidenceText: Arizona]( law deducts amounts received from sales of solar energy devices from the retail tax base and requires the retailer to register as a solar energy retailer.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Keep solar thermal and solar electric categories. Remove the submetering match because the source supports solar devices, not general energy monitoring systems.

geography.notes: Pennsylvania statewide program administered through the Commonwealth Financing Authority.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be an eligible Pennsylvania business, economic development organization, or political subdivision.
Project must qualify under the Alternative and Clean Energy Program rules.
Program financing may require matching funds, application fees, commitment fees, and Commonwealth Financing Authority approval.
blockers: The current official page is the Alternative and Clean Energy Program, not a product-specific solar retrofit rebate.
Do not match rooftop solar PV or solar water heating from this record without a specific source-backed project category.
Pennsylvania Solar Energy Program is a separate solar-specific financing program and should not be merged into this opportunity.
repairs.administrator: Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development
repairs.evidenceText: The]( current DCED page is ACE, a grant, loan, and guarantee program for alternative and clean-energy projects; it does not specifically identify rooftop PV or solar thermal as eligible retrofit products.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Clear retrofit categories to prevent false-positive matches. The official source supports broad clean-energy project financing, not deterministic product-level solar retrofit matching.

geography.notes: Pennsylvania statewide Solar Energy Program loan category administered through the Commonwealth Financing Authority.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be an eligible Pennsylvania business, economic development organization, or political subdivision.
Loan must support an eligible solar energy generation or distribution project or qualifying solar manufacturing activity.
Program loan limits, application fee, loan commitment fee, and matching fund requirements apply.
Storage costs must be directly related to electricity produced by the solar energy system.
blockers: This is financing, not a rebate.
Standalone battery storage is not supported; storage must be tied directly to solar-generated electricity.
Residential homeowner consumer loans are not supported by the official SEP applicant list.
Non-solar energy projects belong under separate Pennsylvania programs.
repairs.administrator: Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development; Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection
repairs.evidenceText: SEP]( loans fund solar energy generation or distribution projects, with storage supported only when directly related to electricity produced by the solar energy system.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Keep solar categories and replace generic battery storage with solar-integrated storage. Do not match standalone storage or consumer-scale residential loans.

geography.notes: Pennsylvania statewide Solar Energy Program grant category administered through the Commonwealth Financing Authority.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be an eligible Pennsylvania business, economic development organization, or political subdivision.
Grant must support an eligible solar energy generation or distribution project or qualifying solar manufacturing activity.
Grant limits, application fee, matching fund requirements, and Commonwealth Financing Authority approval apply.
Photovoltaic grant recipients may have SREC transfer requirements under program rules.
Storage costs must be directly related to electricity produced by the solar energy system.
blockers: This is a grant program, not a rebate for individual homeowners.
Standalone battery storage is not supported; storage must be tied directly to solar-generated electricity.
Non-solar storage, ordinary water heaters, and unrelated clean-energy projects should not match this solar-specific record.
repairs.administrator: Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development; Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection
repairs.evidenceText: SEP]( grants support solar energy generation or distribution projects, and storage is eligible only when directly related to electricity produced by the solar energy system.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Keep solar PV and solar thermal categories. Replace broad battery storage with a solar-integrated storage category and block standalone storage matching.

geography.notes: Minnesota statewide sales-tax exemption for qualifying solar energy systems.

hardRequirements: Purchase must qualify as a solar energy system under Minnesota law.
System must collect, transfer, store, or use solar energy for qualifying thermal or power purposes.
Seller and purchaser must document the nontaxable sale or exemption as required by Minnesota Revenue rules.
blockers: Do not match non-solar water heating, generic thermal storage, or standalone batteries.
Solar storage is only supported when it is part of the solar energy system definition.
Wind, geothermal, and ordinary building-efficiency measures are not supported by this solar-energy sales-tax exemption.
repairs.evidenceText: Minnesota]( Revenue lists solar energy systems as nontaxable sales under the solar-energy-system statutes, supporting solar electric and solar thermal uses.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The rooftop solar PV and solar water heating matches are supported. Add solar space heating because the statutory definition includes solar heating of buildings.

geography.notes: District of Columbia personal property tax exemption for qualifying solar and cogeneration systems.

hardRequirements: Solar system must use exclusively solar energy as defined in District law.
Cogeneration system must produce electrical energy and steam or another useful form of energy such as heat.
Property must be located in the District of Columbia and claimed through applicable personal property tax procedures.
blockers: Generic generators do not qualify unless they meet the cogeneration definition.
Standalone non-solar storage does not qualify.
This is a property tax incentive, not a rebate, grant, or installation financing program.
repairs.administrator: District of Columbia Office of Tax and Revenue
repairs.evidenceText: D.C]( law exempts systems using exclusively solar energy and cogeneration systems that produce electricity plus steam or useful heat for eligible purposes.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The solar thermal and cogeneration matches are supported. Add solar PV because the legal definition of solar energy includes conversion to electrical energy.

geography.notes: Rebates are administered through participating Southern Minnesota Municipal Power Agency member municipal utilities.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be a commercial or industrial electric customer of a participating SMMPA member utility.
Measure must appear on the current local member utility rebate form or qualify through a custom program.
Customer must submit required equipment documentation and utility rebate forms.
Preapproval may be required for some measures.
blockers: Not a residential appliance or home weatherization program.
Energy management should be narrowed to listed guestroom energy management controls or specifically approved custom measures, not broad EMS software or controls.
Refrigeration rebates apply to commercial refrigeration equipment, not household refrigerators.
repairs.evidenceText: SMMPA]( member utility materials list business rebates including refrigeration equipment and guestroom energy management, alongside other commercial and industrial efficiency measures.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The refrigeration match is supported for C&I customers. Narrow the broad energy-management match to guestroom energy-management controls because that is the product-specific official measure.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying Southern Public Power District customers through Nebraska public-power EV incentive channels.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be a Southern Public Power District customer.
Project must install qualifying EV charging infrastructure or make-ready wiring under the current EnergyWise or goEV incentive rules.
Residential charging incentives are limited to qualifying Level 2 charging and make-ready measures.
Nonresidential incentives may include Level 2, DC fast charging, and make-ready infrastructure.
blockers: Not an EV vehicle purchase incentive.
Residential customers should not be matched to DC fast charging unless a current official source explicitly allows it.
Customers outside Southern Public Power District territory do not qualify.
Exact rebate amounts and application details should be verified against the current program portal before quoting.
repairs.evidenceText: The]( goEV site presents residential and commercial EV incentives for Nebraska public-power customers; federal program data lists SPPD charging and make-ready rebates for residential and nonresidential customers.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Level 2 EV charger matching is supported. Added make-ready wiring and nonresidential DC fast charging with medium confidence because the official portal is current but detailed terms are limited.

geography.notes: Program procures SRECs for Delmarva Power compliance from Delaware-certified solar systems; some eligible systems may be in municipal, cooperative, or qualifying out-of-state service territory if certified.

hardRequirements: Applicant must own or control eligible SRECs from a qualifying solar PV system.
System must have or obtain Delaware certification and meet applicable metering or monitoring requirements.
Applications are accepted only during annual procurement windows.
Awarded systems must enter the required long-term SREC transfer agreement.
Applicant must not already have conflicting SREC sale or transfer obligations or incompatible Delaware solar grant arrangements.
blockers: Current procurement window is closed until a future annual solicitation opens.
This is not an upfront solar rebate or equipment discount.
Community solar subscriptions are not the supported match; only qualifying community solar projects or solar system owners may participate.
Net metering is separate from the SREC procurement program.
repairs.administrator: Delaware Sustainable Energy Utility / SREC Delaware Program Administrator for Delmarva Power
repairs.evidenceText: SREC]( Delaware buys SRECs from solar system owners through annual procurement windows; the program requires Delaware certification and SREC ownership or control.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Keep a physical solar PV category and replace community solar subscription with community solar project. Mark temporarily closed because procurements occur in limited annual windows and no current open window was verified.
